--- title: "October 9–13, 2026" date: 2026-10-09 description: "Network median 3.15 in (range 1.14–6.93 in); peak IVT 490 kg m⁻¹ s⁻¹ from the SSW; Rachel within 1,500 km" categories: [IVT ≥ 250, Tropical cyclone nearby, Snow, Final] execute: freeze: auto --- ## Summary Most of the rain fell between Saturday afternoon, October 10, and Monday night, October 12, over about 53 hours. Rain gauges across Flagstaff caught a typical 3.23 inches, from 1.14 in at Flagstaff Landfill to 6.93 in at Waterline Rd #1 (Lenox-Wupatki Trails). The airport measured 3.55 in, about 14 times the normal for those 5 days. Only 3 Octobers since 1898 had a wetter 5 days. Snow fell only at the highest mountain sites; in town it was rain. Nights were mild for the season, about 11 °F above normal. The storm was fed by an atmospheric river, a long, narrow stream of moist air flowing from the south-southwest, drawn north by an area of low pressure aloft centred about 800 miles to the north-northwest. 73% of the rain fell while that stream was overhead. Part of that moisture came directly from the remnants of Rachel, about 230 miles to the west-southwest. 16 of 19 USGS gauges within 68 miles had daily flows above the 90th percentile for the date. Jacks Canyon Creek near Winslow (703 cubic feet per second, or cfs), the Verde River near Camp Verde (10,100 cfs) and the East Verde River near Childs (3,870 cfs) all peaked at about their typical yearly peaks (the median of annual peaks). (River flows are provisional.) ::: {.callout-note collapse="true"} ## Technical summary Across 37 gauges the event total ranged from 1.14 to 6.93 in (median 3.23 in). The central 80% of the network-mean rain fell between Oct 10 16:00 MST and Oct 12 21:00 MST (53 h). Moisture transport over Flagstaff reached atmospheric-river strength: ERA5 IVT was at or above 250 kg m⁻¹ s⁻¹ for 42 h and peaked at 490 kg m⁻¹ s⁻¹ from the SSW at Oct 11 05:00 MST. 73% of the network-mean rain fell while IVT was at or above 250. At the IVT peak, the region of IVT ≥ 250 over Flagstaff was continuous with the area around Rachel (remnant disturbance, 33.9°N 115.4°W, 373 km to the WSW). At the IVT peak, 500-hPa flow over Flagstaff was from the SSW at 35 m s⁻¹, and the 500-hPa trough axis along 35.25°N was at 122.2°W, 963 km west of Flagstaff (5,619 m, against 5,716 m over Flagstaff). A closed 500-hPa low (5,470 m) was centred 1,289 km to the NNW, at 45.2°N 119.2°W. The strongest 250-hPa wind within 1,000 km was 63 m s⁻¹, 958 km to the N. The 250-hPa wind over Flagstaff peaked at 62 m s⁻¹ (Oct 12 23:00 MST), 42 h after the IVT peak. ::: ## Rain across the network ::: {#89530c80 .cell execution_count=3} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ![Event rain total at each city and county gauge (circle color and label show the total in inches; map cropped to the network) over shaded relief (USGS 3DEP), 200-m elevation contours, streams (USGS NHD) and highways (Census TIGER). Tap or click the map to open the frame full size.* ## What the forecasters said The National Weather Service office in Flagstaff discussed the moisture source in its Area Forecast Discussions as the event unfolded. Excerpts, quoted verbatim (links to the Iowa Environmental Mesonet archive): - **Oct 8, 2:42 AM MST** ([AFD](https://mesonet.agron.iastate.edu/wx/afos/p.php?pil=AFDFGZ&e=202610080942)): "As the trough digs south, it will interact with what will become the remnants of TS Rachel." - **Oct 10, 10:48 AM MST** ([AFD](https://mesonet.agron.iastate.edu/wx/afos/p.php?pil=AFDFGZ&e=202610101748)): "Tropical Storm Rachel, about 500 miles southwest of San Diego as of 8 AM MST, is quickly moving northward as it begins to be pulled northward by an upper-level low off the California coast." - **Oct 11, 3:01 AM MST** ([AFD](https://mesonet.agron.iastate.edu/wx/afos/p.php?pil=AFDFGZ&e=202610111001)): "After making landfall earlier this evening, the remnants of Tropical Storm Rachel are moving towards the north- northeast early this morning before exiting into Utah this afternoon. … With a continued strong southerly flow, moisture has continued to advect into the region and have left ripe conditions with the potential for heavy rain through today." - **Oct 11, 11:25 AM MST** ([AFD](https://mesonet.agron.iastate.edu/wx/afos/p.php?pil=AFDFGZ&e=202610111825)): "Moisture from Hurricane Rachel has moved into much of northern Arizona this morning, with PWAT values near or exceeding daily record levels." ## Climate context - **Airport precipitation:** 3.55 in over 5 local days, against a 1991–2020 normal of 0.25 in for those days (14× normal). - **Rank:** the 4th largest 5-day airport total in October among 129 years with data since 1898 (each year's largest 5-day total ending in October). - **Airport temperature:** highs averaged -5.2 °F and lows +10.6 °F relative to normal. - **Water year to date** (Oct 1, 2026 – Oct 13, 2026): airport 3.55 in (normal 0.62 in);
